newsitem.title: USA: X.L. Insurance to buy American Excess assets.
newsitem.headline: X.L. Insurance to buy American Excess assets.

text.p: X.L. Insurance Co Ltd has entered into agreement to buy the assets of the American Excess Insurance Association for an undisclosed sum, the association said on Wednesday.
American Excess, an association of 13 major U.S. insurance copanies, would dissolve in the near future, American Excess President John Traynor said.

"At a time when an expanding marketplace and insurance industry consolidations have produced higher limits and broader product availability, the member companies of AEIA have decided to refocus their resources on other areas of the marketplace," Traynor said in a statement.
X.L. Insurance Co, owned by Bermuda-based EXEL Ltd, agreed to offer renewals in Bermuda to the Association's policyholders through Bermuda intermediaries, American Excess said.

American Excess specialized in providing up to $100 million in excess third party liabilty coverage over a minimun attachment of $25 million, it said. Its annual premium in 1995 was $47 million, it said.
